title: Word Segmentation
statement:
Decide whether a string can be cut into a sequence of dictionary words.

Contract
- `text` is non-null and may be empty. `dictionary` is non-null, may be empty, and holds
  non-empty words that may repeat.
- Return `true` when `text` can be split into one or more consecutive pieces, in order and with
  nothing left over, where every piece is a word from `dictionary`. Words may be used any number
  of times. An empty `text` needs no pieces and is segmentable.
- Matching is case-sensitive. Do not mutate `dictionary`.

Examples
- `canSegment("applepie", List.of("apple", "pie"))` returns `true`.
- `canSegment("abcd", List.of("a", "abc", "b", "cd"))` returns `true` ("a", "b", "cd").
- `canSegment("abce", List.of("abc", "d"))` returns `false`.
hints: Taking the longest matching word at the front can lead to a dead end. Consider every word that matches a prefix.
Let reachable[i] mean the first i characters can be segmented. Position i is reachable if some earlier reachable position j has text[j..i) in the dictionary.

Put the words in a hash set and only look back as far as the longest word. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space for a dictionary whose words have bounded length, where n is the length of the text (in general O(n * longest word length)).
inputSyntax: Input: the text followed by the dictionary words in brackets, for example: applepie [apple, pie]
